verdict.rationale: Gram documents OAuth support for its MCP servers: a guide covers building a server with external OAuth authentication using any OAuth 2.0 provider. Governed third-party endpoints also apply upstream credentials without changes to the upstream. Neither source shows the platform brokering downstream OAuth flows end to end, and secure vaulting and refresh are not mentioned at all. missing for 10: evidence the platform itself runs OAuth flows for downstream tools, encrypted credential vaulting, automatic token refresh, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can let the platform run OAuth flows for downstream tools and vault the resulting credentials encrypted, with automatic token refresh

citations.quote: This guide shows you how to build an MCP server with external OAuth authentication.
you can use any OAuth 2.0 provider you have set up (such as Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, or your own OAuth server)
so access control, audit, and upstream credentials apply without changing the upstream
